# STM32H743 AIO Flight Controller with 4-in-1 80A ESC: Systems Architecture Model (Job #19)

## 0. Scope, Assumptions and Design Flags

**Architecture.** On an AIO "nano" board, the STM32H743 runs ArduPilot and generates bidirectional DShot600. The 48 kHz bridge PWM is generated by four dedicated ESC MCUs, not by the H743. The reference ESC MCU is the AT32F421 or STM32G071 running AM32.

**Assumptions** (replace with your datasheet values and re-run the equations):

| Parameter | Symbol | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Bus voltage (6S, worst case) | V_bus | 25.2 V |
| MOSFET (40 V, 5×6 DFN class) | R_ds(on),25 | 1.0 mΩ max @ V_gs = 10 V |
| | Q_g / Q_gs2 / Q_gd | 60 / 8 / 12 nC |
| | Q_rr @ 80 A | 80 nC |
| | Q_oss | 40 nC |
| | V_plateau | 3.5 V |
| | R_g,int | 1 Ω |
| | R_θJC | 0.8 K/W |
| Gate driver | V_drv | 10 V |
| | R_source / R_sink | 3 Ω / 1 Ω |
| External gate resistor | R_g,ext | 2 Ω |
| Dead time | t_dt | 200 ns per edge |
| Body diode forward voltage | V_f | 0.8 V |
| Board | — | 30.5 × 30.5 mm, 6-layer, 2 oz, one MOSFET per switch |
| Commutation | — | 6-step trapezoidal, PWM on one leg; second leg low-side on |

**Design flags:**
- **80A is a burst rating only on a nano board.** The thermal model below gives about 25A continuous per channel. All four channels at 80A simultaneously is limited to roughly 1.4 s.
- **Motor pins need non-complementary timer channels.** Bidirectional DShot requires input capture, which ArduPilot cannot do on CHxN outputs.

## 1. Conduction Loss Model

### 1.1 Temperature-dependent R_ds(on)

$$R_{ds}(T_j) = R_{ds,25}\,[1 + \alpha (T_j - 25)],\quad \alpha \approx 0.0045\ \text{K}^{-1}$$

At T_j = 125 °C: R_ds = 1.0 mΩ × 1.45 ≈ **1.5 mΩ** (design value).

### 1.2 Per-leg and per-channel conduction

In a synchronous complementary leg, the high side conducts for fraction D and the low side for (1 − D):

$$P_{cond,leg} = I^2 R_{ds} D + I^2 R_{ds}(1-D) = I^2 R_{ds}$$

The result is independent of duty cycle. With two legs carrying current in each commutation step:

$$P_{cond,ch} = 2 I^2 R_{ds}(T_j)$$

At 80A: P_cond,ch = 2 × 6400 × 1.5 mΩ = **19.2 W**, of which **9.6 W** is in the hottest FET.

### 1.3 PCB copper loss

2 oz copper has a sheet resistance R_□ ≈ 0.245 mΩ/□ at 25 °C, about 0.34 mΩ/□ at 125 °C.

For the battery-to-phase path, assume about 3 squares paralleled across 4 inner and outer layers:

R_Cu ≈ 3 × 0.34 / 4 ≈ 0.26 mΩ, giving P_Cu ≈ 80² × 0.26 mΩ ≈ **1.7 W** per channel.
